work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Fourth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. Westminster. The Jerusalem Chamber.

content.text: Enter the King, Warwick, Thomas Duke of Clarence and Humphrey Duke of Gloucester and others.

lines.text: Now, lords, if God doth give successful end
lines.plainText: Now lords if God doth give successful end

lines.text: To this debate that bleedeth at our doors,
lines.plainText: To this debate that bleedeth at our doors

lines.text: We will our youth lead on to higher fields
lines.plainText: We will our youth lead on to higher fields

lines.text: And draw no swords but what are sanctified.
lines.plainText: And draw no swords but what are sanctified

lines.text: Our navy is address'd, our power collected,
lines.plainText: Our navy is address'd our power collected

lines.text: Our substitutes in absence well invested,
lines.plainText: Our substitutes in absence well invested

lines.text: And everything lies level to our wish.
lines.plainText: And everything lies level to our wish

lines.text: Only we want a little personal strength;
lines.plainText: Only we want a little personal strength

lines.text: And pause us till these rebels now afoot
lines.plainText: And pause us till these rebels now afoot

lines.text: Come underneath the yoke of government.
lines.plainText: Come underneath the yoke of government

lines.text: Both which we doubt not but your Majesty
lines.plainText: Both which we doubt not but your Majesty

lines.text: Shall soon enjoy.
lines.plainText: Shall soon enjoy

lines.text: Humphrey, my son of Gloucester,
lines.plainText: Humphrey my son of Gloucester

lines.text: Where is the Prince your brother?
lines.plainText: Where is the Prince your brother

lines.text: I think he's gone to hunt, my lord, at Windsor.
lines.plainText: I think he's gone to hunt my lord at Windsor

lines.text: And how accompanied?
lines.plainText: And how accompanied

lines.text: I do not know, my lord.
lines.plainText: I do not know my lord

lines.text: Is not his brother Thomas of Clarence with him?
lines.plainText: Is not his brother Thomas of Clarence with him

lines.text: No, my good lord, he is in presence here.
lines.plainText: No my good lord he is in presence here

lines.text: What would my lord and father?
lines.plainText: What would my lord and father

lines.text: Nothing but well to thee, Thomas of Clarence.
lines.plainText: Nothing but well to thee Thomas of Clarence

lines.text: How chance thou art not with the Prince thy brother?
lines.plainText: How chance thou art not with the Prince thy brother

lines.text: He loves thee, and thou dost neglect him, Thomas.
lines.plainText: He loves thee and thou dost neglect him Thomas

lines.text: Thou hast a better place in his affection
lines.plainText: Thou hast a better place in his affection

lines.text: Than all thy brothers. Cherish it, my boy,
lines.plainText: Than all thy brothers Cherish it my boy

lines.text: And noble offices thou mayst effect
lines.plainText: And noble offices thou mayst effect

lines.text: Of mediation, after I am dead,
lines.plainText: Of mediation after I am dead

lines.text: Between his greatness and thy other brethren.
lines.plainText: Between his greatness and thy other brethren

lines.text: Therefore omit him not, blunt not his love,
lines.plainText: Therefore omit him not blunt not his love

lines.text: Nor lose the good advantage of his grace
lines.plainText: Nor lose the good advantage of his grace

lines.text: By seeming cold or careless of his will;
lines.plainText: By seeming cold or careless of his will

lines.text: For he is gracious, if he be observed,
lines.plainText: For he is gracious if he be observed

lines.text: He hath a tear for pity, and a hand
lines.plainText: He hath a tear for pity and a hand

lines.text: Open as day for melting charity:
lines.plainText: Open as day for melting charity

lines.text: Yet notwithstanding, being incensed, he's flint,
lines.plainText: Yet notwithstanding being incensed he's flint

lines.text: As humorous as winter, and as sudden
lines.plainText: As humorous as winter and as sudden

lines.text: As flaws congealed in the spring of day.
lines.plainText: As flaws congealed in the spring of day

lines.text: His temper therefore must be well observed.
lines.plainText: His temper therefore must be well observed

lines.text: Chide him for faults, and do it reverently,
lines.plainText: Chide him for faults and do it reverently

lines.text: When you perceive his blood inclined to mirth;
lines.plainText: When you perceive his blood inclined to mirth

lines.text: But, being moody, give him time and scope,
lines.plainText: But being moody give him time and scope

lines.text: Till that his passions, like a whale on ground,
lines.plainText: Till that his passions like a whale on ground

lines.text: Confound themselves with working. Learn this, Thomas,
lines.plainText: Confound themselves with working Learn this Thomas

lines.text: And thou shalt prove a shelter to thy friends,
lines.plainText: And thou shalt prove a shelter to thy friends

lines.text: A hoop of gold to bind thy brothers in,
lines.plainText: A hoop of gold to bind thy brothers in

lines.text: That the united vessel of their blood,
lines.plainText: That the united vessel of their blood

lines.text: Mingled with venom of suggestion—
lines.plainText: Mingled with venom of suggestion

lines.text: As, force perforce, the age will pour it in—
lines.plainText: As force perforce the age will pour it in

lines.text: Shall never leak, though it do work as strong
lines.plainText: Shall never leak though it do work as strong

lines.text: As aconitum or rash gunpowder.
lines.plainText: As aconitum or rash gunpowder

lines.text: I shall observe him with all care and love.
lines.plainText: I shall observe him with all care and love

lines.text: Why art thou not at Windsor with him, Thomas?
lines.plainText: Why art thou not at Windsor with him Thomas

lines.text: He is not there today; he dines in London.
lines.plainText: He is not there today he dines in London

lines.text: And how accompanied? Canst thou tell that?
lines.plainText: And how accompanied Canst thou tell that

lines.text: With Poins, and other his continual followers.
lines.plainText: With Poins and other his continual followers

lines.text: Most subject is the fattest soil to weeds,
lines.plainText: Most subject is the fattest soil to weeds

lines.text: And he, the noble image of my youth,
lines.plainText: And he the noble image of my youth

lines.text: Is overspread with them; therefore my grief
lines.plainText: Is overspread with them therefore my grief

lines.text: Stretches itself beyond the hour of death.
lines.plainText: Stretches itself beyond the hour of death

lines.text: The blood weeps from my heart when I do shape
lines.plainText: The blood weeps from my heart when I do shape

lines.text: In forms imaginary th' unguided days
lines.plainText: In forms imaginary th' unguided days

lines.text: And rotten times that you shall look upon
lines.plainText: And rotten times that you shall look upon

lines.text: When I am sleeping with my ancestors.
lines.plainText: When I am sleeping with my ancestors

lines.text: For when his headstrong riot hath no curb,
lines.plainText: For when his headstrong riot hath no curb

lines.text: When rage and hot blood are his counsellors,
lines.plainText: When rage and hot blood are his counsellors

lines.text: When means and lavish manners meet together,
lines.plainText: When means and lavish manners meet together

lines.text: O, with what wings shall his affections fly
lines.plainText: O with what wings shall his affections fly

lines.text: Towards fronting peril and opposed decay!
lines.plainText: Towards fronting peril and opposed decay

lines.text: My gracious lord, you look beyond him quite.
lines.plainText: My gracious lord you look beyond him quite

lines.text: The prince but studies his companions
lines.plainText: The prince but studies his companions

lines.text: Like a strange tongue, wherein, to gain the language,
lines.plainText: Like a strange tongue wherein to gain the language

lines.text: 'Tis needful that the most immodest word
lines.plainText: 'Tis needful that the most immodest word

lines.text: Be looked upon and learned; which once attained,
lines.plainText: Be looked upon and learned which once attained

lines.text: Your Highness knows, comes to no further use
lines.plainText: Your Highness knows comes to no further use

lines.text: But to be known and hated. So, like gross terms,
lines.plainText: But to be known and hated So like gross terms

lines.text: The Prince will, in the perfectness of time,
lines.plainText: The Prince will in the perfectness of time

lines.text: Cast off his followers, and their memory
lines.plainText: Cast off his followers and their memory

lines.text: Shall as a pattern or a measure live,
lines.plainText: Shall as a pattern or a measure live

lines.text: By which his Grace must mete the lives of other,
lines.plainText: By which his Grace must mete the lives of other

lines.text: Turning past evils to advantages.
lines.plainText: Turning past evils to advantages

lines.text: 'Tis seldom when the bee doth leave her comb
lines.plainText: 'Tis seldom when the bee doth leave her comb

lines.text: In the dead carrion.
lines.plainText: In the dead carrion

lines.text: Health to my sovereign, and new happiness
lines.plainText: Health to my sovereign and new happiness

lines.text: Added to that that I am to deliver!
lines.plainText: Added to that that I am to deliver

lines.text: Prince John your son doth kiss your Grace's hand.
lines.plainText: Prince John your son doth kiss your Grace's hand

lines.text: Mowbray, the Bishop Scroop, Hastings and all
lines.plainText: Mowbray the Bishop Scroop Hastings and all

lines.text: Are brought to the correction of your law.
lines.plainText: Are brought to the correction of your law

lines.text: There is not now a rebel's sword unsheathed,
lines.plainText: There is not now a rebel's sword unsheathed

lines.text: But Peace puts forth her olive everywhere.
lines.plainText: But Peace puts forth her olive everywhere

lines.text: The manner how this action hath been borne
lines.plainText: The manner how this action hath been borne

lines.text: Here at more leisure may your Highness read,
lines.plainText: Here at more leisure may your Highness read

lines.text: With every course in his particular.
lines.plainText: With every course in his particular

lines.text: O Westmoreland, thou art a summer bird,
lines.plainText: O Westmoreland thou art a summer bird

lines.text: Which ever in the haunch of winter sings
lines.plainText: Which ever in the haunch of winter sings

lines.text: The lifting up of day.
lines.plainText: The lifting up of day

lines.text: From enemies heaven keep your Majesty;
lines.plainText: From enemies heaven keep your Majesty

lines.text: And when they stand against you, may they fall
lines.plainText: And when they stand against you may they fall

lines.text: As those that I am come to tell you of!
lines.plainText: As those that I am come to tell you of

lines.text: The Earl Northumberland and the Lord Bardolph,
lines.plainText: The Earl Northumberland and the Lord Bardolph

lines.text: With a great power of English and of Scots,
lines.plainText: With a great power of English and of Scots

lines.text: Are by the shrieve of Yorkshire overthrown.
lines.plainText: Are by the shrieve of Yorkshire overthrown

lines.text: The manner and true order of the fight
lines.plainText: The manner and true order of the fight

lines.text: This packet, please it you, contains at large.
lines.plainText: This packet please it you contains at large

lines.text: And wherefore should these good news make me sick?
lines.plainText: And wherefore should these good news make me sick

lines.text: Will Fortune never come with both hands full,
lines.plainText: Will Fortune never come with both hands full

lines.text: But write her fair words still in foulest letters?
lines.plainText: But write her fair words still in foulest letters

lines.text: She either gives a stomach and no food—
lines.plainText: She either gives a stomach and no food

lines.text: Such are the poor, in health; or else a feast
lines.plainText: Such are the poor in health or else a feast

lines.text: And takes away the stomach—such are the rich,
lines.plainText: And takes away the stomachsuch are the rich

lines.text: That have abundance and enjoy it not.
lines.plainText: That have abundance and enjoy it not

lines.text: I should rejoice now at this happy news,
lines.plainText: I should rejoice now at this happy news

lines.text: And now my sight fails, and my brain is giddy.
lines.plainText: And now my sight fails and my brain is giddy

lines.text: O me! Come near me, now I am much ill.
lines.plainText: O me Come near me now I am much ill

lines.text: Comfort, your Majesty!
lines.plainText: Comfort your Majesty

lines.text: O my royal father!
lines.plainText: O my royal father

lines.text: My sovereign lord, cheer up yourself, look up.
lines.plainText: My sovereign lord cheer up yourself look up

lines.text: Be patient, princes; you do know these fits
lines.plainText: Be patient princes you do know these fits

lines.text: Are with his Highness very ordinary.
lines.plainText: Are with his Highness very ordinary

lines.text: Stand from him, give him air; he'll straight be well.
lines.plainText: Stand from him give him air he'll straight be well

lines.text: No, no, he cannot long hold out these pangs.
lines.plainText: No no he cannot long hold out these pangs

lines.text: Th' incessant care and labour of his mind
lines.plainText: Th' incessant care and labour of his mind

lines.text: Hath wrought the mure that should confine it in
lines.plainText: Hath wrought the mure that should confine it in

lines.text: So thin that life looks through and will break out.
lines.plainText: So thin that life looks through and will break out

lines.text: The people fear me, for they do observe
lines.plainText: The people fear me for they do observe

lines.text: Unfather'd heirs and loathly births of nature.
lines.plainText: Unfather'd heirs and loathly births of nature

lines.text: The seasons change their manners, as the year
lines.plainText: The seasons change their manners as the year

lines.text: Had found some months asleep and leap'd them over.
lines.plainText: Had found some months asleep and leap'd them over

lines.text: The river hath thrice flow'd, no ebb between,
lines.plainText: The river hath thrice flow'd no ebb between

lines.text: And the old folk, time's doting chronicles,
lines.plainText: And the old folk time's doting chronicles

lines.text: Say it did so a little time before
lines.plainText: Say it did so a little time before

lines.text: That our great-grandsire, Edward, sick'd and died.
lines.plainText: That our greatgrandsire Edward sick'd and died

lines.text: Speak lower, princes, for the King recovers.
lines.plainText: Speak lower princes for the King recovers

lines.text: This apoplexy will certain be his end.
lines.plainText: This apoplexy will certain be his end

lines.text: I pray you take me up, and bear me hence
lines.plainText: I pray you take me up and bear me hence

lines.text: Into some other chamber: softly, pray.
lines.plainText: Into some other chamber softly pray
